::: {.why}
If the two disagree, that disagreement is the most interesting result of the year and it goes at the front of the capstone, because it is the only genuinely out-of-sample evidence you have.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Decompose the difference between live and backtested returns into signal, execution and universe components.
- Say which component was largest and whether you would have predicted it.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Decompose it properly rather than attributing it to noise: run the backtest with the live period's actual fills substituted for its modelled fills, which isolates execution, then with the live universe substituted, which isolates selection. What remains is signal difference plus noise, and the three parts should sum to the total.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Check the prediction: your milestone 5 list of lies ranked what would matter most, and this decomposition is the first real test of that ranking. Report whether the largest component was where you predicted, and update the list either way.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The live-against-backtest difference is decomposed into execution, universe and signal components that sum to the total, which is the first empirical test of the ranked list of lies from milestone 5.
:::
